summary: The note looks at the people behind a local music scene, mainly producers and promoters, and how they shape its sound since a small-venue resurgence began in September 2023. It covers producer tools and collaboration, promoter networking and venue scouting, the role of social media, community involvement, and festivals. It closes with challenges such as gentrification and financial instability, and a look ahead to VR and AI in music.
one_line: A look at the producers and promoters who shape the local music scene, covering their work, tools, challenges and the future of local sound.
key_facts: Since September 2023, small, intimate venues have seen a resurgence as audiences crave live, personalized performances.
On October 15, 2023, local producer Jeremy Reynolds released the collaborative EP "Echoes from the Alleyway," showcasing emerging talent from the neighborhood of Eastwood.
Jeremy Reynolds likens a producer to a chef: "the ingredients might be the same, but it's the recipe and technique that create a new exciting dish every time."
Popular Digital Audio Workstations among budding producers are Ableton Live, FL Studio, and Logic Pro X; headphones, studio monitors and MIDI controllers are also part of the toolkit.
As of November 2023, music equipment stores reported a spike in demand for home studio gear, reflecting the rise of bedroom producers.
On September 20, 2023, producer Melissa Huang hosted the first of a series of community center workshops pairing instrumentalists with aspiring producers.
Anna Clarke, associated with the indie rock revival in midtown, was responsible for the October Fest series that brought record numbers to local venues throughout 2023.
Promoter Jameson O'Reilly brought a wave of electronic acts to smaller venues in Spring 2023.
On December 3, 2023, the Eastwood Music Collective launched a food drive alongside their winter concert series.
The annual festival Midtown Sounds debuted on September 2, 2023, helping establish a rhythm to the local music calendar.
Challenges for the scene include gentrification eroding performance spaces and the financial instability of an arts career.
Towards the end of 2023, talk of enhanced VR music experiences and AI-assisted music production was circulating.
